preview: Mohammed Bhadsorawala shares his Goldman Sachs Summer Analyst internship interview experience for the 2024 drive, detailing the online assessment, technical and HR interview rounds, and preparation tips.
content: GOLDMAN SACHS SUMMER ANALYST INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE YEAR - 2024 MOHAMMED BHADSORAWALA COMPUTER ENGINEERING BATCH - 2026 Introduction Hello readers, myself Mohammed Bhadsorawala, TY CS student at VJTI. Well today at least I am proud about VJTI for the on-campus internship opportunities we get. Today I would like to share my overall internship drive experience with you all. The internship drive started in SY March with JPMC with their Online Assessment (OA). Our seniors told us that JPMC OA is very easy but for most of us it wasn’t. The OA consisted of Medium to Hard CP & DSA Problems. Around April I think we had 2nd online round of JPMC (More details about the process in JPMC experiences). I was fortunate to be selected for JPMC Code For Good. For 14-15 June, we went to JPMC Office, it was a great experience stepping into the corporate experience and JPMC was very hostile and cared for us as “Hone wale Damad”. I would like to say that never think that “JPMC isn’t the best company, better companies will come in future so I won’t be very serious about JPMC”. Give your best shot for each opportunity. At JPMC Hackathon, I was confident and voiced my opinions in front of the team and the mentors and tried my best to set a good impression. We had thought that our internship season would begin in August with our TY and had the perception that we had enough time to prepare. But in June end, we were informed that DE Shaw and Google would be coming for internships in July start. For DE Shaw, I was shortlisted, gave my first interview, it went well, but I wasn’t called for the second round. For Google, I wasn’t shortlisted after the OA but I saw that few people who solved lesser than me, were shortlisted (dard*=2). Google OA was tough but interview questions were easier, at least in Round 1 (I was like mujhe kyu toda phir OA me :) ). Google only asked DSA questions and no CS fundamentals. It was a tough phase, but rejections at this stage of life are important to help us prepare for any setback in life ahead. Then 10 days earlier, Goldman Sachs drive was announced. I read all interview experiences of past 3-4 years and got an understanding of the mindset of GS interviewers. For banks, always wear formals for the interview, also prepare well for HR questions. I would suggest, don’t write and memorise your HR questions. Read few answers online, ask ChatGPT but then make sure you have some personal unique touch in your answers. Don’t give them the answers they are listening for years already. So now lets begin GS interview process Pre Placement Talk Somewhere around 12 July 2024, we received an email from TPO informing us that Goldman Sachs was visiting the campus for intern hiring. In this email, there were links for applying on the official Goldman Sachs Careers page as well as details for a webinar. Platform: Zoom Webinar. Time: 23 July 2024, 5pm - 6pm. The Pre-Placement Talk was engaging and to the point. They started off by explaining what GS does, why GS stands out from the rest and what kind of lifestyle you can expect at GS. Pay close attention to whatever is discussed in this meeting, as it serves as a good way to understand the kind of people the firm is looking for. Additionally, during your interviews, the interviewers may ask you questions about the firm, and the insights shared in this session can help you make a strong impression. Preparing for this talk and taking detailed notes will definitely pay off in the later stages of the hiring process. For any company, its values and missions are important. So understand their values and try to incorporate that in your HR answers because most of others wont do this. I used to take notes of Pre Placement talk and go through them before the interview day. Online Assessment Platform - Hackerank (Video and Screen proctored) Duration - Around 1 hour The online assessment consisted of: 10 multiple-choice questions (MCQs) -15 mins 3 coding questions - 40 mins 1 HR-related questions - 5mins As much as I remember, we were allocated 55 minutes to complete the MCQs and coding questions, and an additional 5 minutes for the HR questions. Each MCQ earns you 3 marks for correct answer and -1 mark for incorrect answer. Coding Questions - 3 Questions 1) Modest Number The problem is to identify modest numbers within a given range (inclusive of start and end). A number is considered modest if it can be split into two parts (left and right), such that dividing the number by the right part gives a remainder equal to the left part. The program should check all possible combinations of left and right partitions of a number to verify this condition. Solution Approach 1. Splitting Numbers: Iterate over all digits of a number to partition it into left and right parts. 2. Validation: Check if the right part is non-zero and if the condition number % right == left holds. 3. Iterate Over Range: For every number in the given range, apply the above check. 4. Output: Collect and print all numbers that satisfy the modest number property. This approach ensures all possible partitions are tested for each number within the range. 2) Identifying Unique Colors on Painting Sheets Problem: You are given N rectangular painting sheets and M shots. Each sheet is defined by four integers representing the bottom-left and top-right corners of the rectangle, i.e., (x1, y1) and (x2, y2). Each shot has a set of coordinates (x, y) and a color. The goal is to determine, for each sheet, how many unique colors have been shot within the boundaries of that sheet. For each shot, you need to check if the shot's coordinates lie within the bounds of each painting sheet. If the shot is within a sheet, the color of that shot should be considered for that sheet. Input: N (number of painting sheets) and M (number of shots). N rectangles, each defined by four integers (x1, y1, x2, y2), representing the coordinates of the bottom-left and top-right corners. M shots, each defined by three integers: (x, y) for the coordinates and color for the color of the shot. Output: For each sheet, output the number of unique colors that have been shot within the sheet's bounds. Solution Approach: 1. Store Sheet Data: Each sheet is represented by a rectangle with four coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2). 2. Track Unique Colors: For each shot, check if the shot’s coordinates fall within the bounds of each sheet. If they do, add the color of the shot to the respective sheet's set. 3. Output: After processing all shots, the size of each sheet’s set will give the number of unique colors associated with that sheet. This approach efficiently uses sets to ensure that only unique colors are counted for each sheet. 3) Card The problem involved using a greedy approach and working with arrays. While I can't recall the exact details of the question, it revolved around distributing or sorting cards in some way that required an optimal solution using a greedy strategy. The task likely involved finding a way to minimize or maximize certain values based on the cards' properties (such as their values, positions, or some other attributes). MCQs - 10 Questions 1. Blocks of Different Colours Flock Together: This problem involves calculating the probability of selecting three balls of different colors from a box containing white, black, and red balls, given certain relationships between the number of balls of each color. 2. Printer and Bookshelf Efficiency: This scenario involves a printer and a bookshelf with various operations like printing papers, stacking books, and handling failures (paper getting stuck or books falling down), represented by different operations (X, Y, Z, W). 3. Binary Tree Check: This question is about the properties of a complete binary tree, where you need to identify the correct statement related to the structure and characteristics of a complete binary tree. 4. Reality TV: In this problem, you're asked to calculate the number of ways to form a group of six people from eight teams, ensuring that exactly one team's both members are selected. 5. Probability Games: This question involves selecting three balls from a box containing prime numbers from 1 to 30 and finding the probability that the sum of their numbers is even and their product is less than 500. 6. Sequence Check: This problem asks you to verify or identify properties of a given sequence of numbers or elements. 7. Binary Tree Nodes: This question likely asks about the properties or characteristics related to the number of nodes in a binary tree and how they are structured. 8. Multiple Inheritance: This question tests knowledge about multiple inheritance in object-oriented programming, particularly in terms of how it works and the challenges associated with it. 9. Queue-Stack Time: This question is about analyzing the time complexity of insertions and deletions in a queue, given a specific number of push and pop operations. 10. Linked List: This problem involves operations on a linked list, testing knowledge of how linked lists function and the operations that can be performed on them. HR Question - 1 Question The question was how I would ensure a smooth transition of responsibilities if I were leaving a team. Specifically, the question was: "If you are leaving a team, how will you make sure you communicate all the important details and responsibilities to another team member?" The focus was on how to effectively transfer knowledge and tasks to ensure the continuity of the team's work. Results: 27 people were shortlisted for interviews, and I was one of them. We received the results on 25 July 2024, in the afternoon. Start preparing for the interviews as soon as you are done with the OA. Don’t wait for the results as they are always announced only the day before interviews. Interview Day Date: 26 July 2024 Venue: TPO Seminar Hall Well 25 July was the day of Red Alert in Mumbai and we were hoping that interviews can be shifted the online but it didn’t happen. The day started with a reporting time of 8:30 am, followed by the Pre-Interview Talk scheduled at 9:00 am. We were instructed to bring 3-4 printouts of our resumes and dress formally. I wore a blue shirt(I heard somewhere that blue colour builds belief), black trousers, a belt, and formal shoes. Dressing well is crucial (Halo effect), especially when interviewing with financial firms, so make sure to present yourself professionally. A team of around 6-7 people from GS was responsible for managing the process. About five of them were engineers from GS, while the rest were HR/Managerial personnel. During the Pre-Interview Talk, they gave us an overview of the interview procedure and their roles at GS. They explained that the interview would consist of technical rounds followed by HR rounds. After the Pre-Interview talk they wait for any questions from us. Now this is a very interesting situation. You must stand out from everyone else and ask questions to show that you are courageous and brave enough to voice out loud. And also you shouldn’t ask a very generic or common question that would show them that you are asking this just for the sake of asking. You must also not ask something they have talked about in Pre Placement Talk 2 days ago(I would really judge someone for this). So after 1-2 people asked their questions, I asked a question prepared within few seconds. After the talk, the interview process began around 10 am without any delays. A few important tips to keep in mind before the interview: 1. Ask about the company: Show your interest by asking questions regarding the technologies the company is working on or other relevant aspects of the organization. 2. Research the company: Before the interview, make sure to gather background details about the company, including its latest news and collaborations. This will help you stand out as an informed candidate and show your genuine interest. Round 1: Technical Interview (Duration: 25-30 min) The interviews began at 10 am and 3 interviewers would taking interview parallelly. I was called in the first 3. Before the interview/exams, I forget all the worries and take a confident walk with some motivational music sometimes. The interviewer wants to select you and they would believe in you only if you believe in yourself. Everyone is nervous for the interview but I prefer to think that the person isn’t an interviewer but a junior I am explaining the code logic/concept to. Always take deep breaths, calm yourself down and enter for the interview thinking YOU ARE THE BEST and they need employees like you more than you need them. I tried my best to be excited and entered the interview room with a smile. My interviewer(she) made sure I am comfortable. She started reading my resume and was looking impressed with my HSC(HSC Mumbai Topper 96.83%) CET(99.96%ile State Rank 35) scores and CGPA (9.66 then and decreasing henceforth :) ) So good cgpa can have a psychological impression on the interviewer. She asked what are my hobbies other than coding. Well I didn’t have any artistic hobby but make sure to make a mention if you have one as this can be a differentiating factor. She started going through my resume, she didn’t ask for proper introduction so I asked her if I should. I gave my well prepared introduction(you should always have one for good first impression). The interviewer would judge you based on your introduction. She saw my projects and asked a question, explain like the way you would explain to your junior not knowing much about the technology. So she started with the DSA question, she drew a tree with people names as nodes Ramesh / \ Suresh Priya / \ / \ Ananya Aarav Kavya Nikhil She: What is this Me: It’s a tree She : Which tree Me : Currently it’s a binary Tree She : Yeah so this is a BST Me: Okay She said that this is a employee hierarchy in a company, how would you remove suresh so that the tree is balanced. I asked questions to clarify what she wants and then she drew a BST with numbers and asked for deletion of a mid level node. The example she gave with simple but I knew that this problem, Deletion in BST do have many edge cases .I kept on talking about my approach, taking edge cases by myself and refining the approach as we progressed. She asked me to write pseudo code, I wrote the main logic on paper(Do take a working pen with you for the interview). She asked if I had any questions for her. I was surprised that the interview ended too soon, I asked 1-2 good questions and left with a Thank You. So taking edges cases by yourself would have a very good impression on your interview and may end your interview with lesser questions. I went to tpo hall to realise that I am the first one to come back from the interview.I talked to everyone explaining my experience and question. Within 5-10 minutes, I was called again and waited outside taking deep breaths. (I was first one to called for round 2 ) Round 2: (Duration: 20 mins) Now X was the managing director of GS, he spoke during PPT as well. They all came from Hyderabad for the drive during peak Mumbai Mansoon. I was expecting for a Round 2 similar to round 1 but was surprised to see X as the interviewer. He read through my resume, I again had to ask myself for giving introduction (It was interviewer’s first interview so maybe they forgot to ask introdution). He asked me to explain my journey to VJTI. I spoke about HSC success(never missing the HSC Topper flex) and change of plans, giving 6 entrance exams, scoring not the best in them until CET and facing decision fatigue on which college to choose. He then asked What is your biggest achievement. This was again shocking as I didn’t expect this to be an HR round but I was prepared for this question. He then asked, there are so many problems in Mumbai, how can you solve them. I said as you must have travelled from airport, you would have seen roads, potholes & drainage problems and elaborating on that. I did focus on the implementation, system design and scalability problems related to my solutions. I think I answered good enough for them. He asked do you have any questions, I mentioned about Microsoft Crowdstrike issue (18-19 July 2024) as it happened few days ago and asked how do GS takes care that such problems don’t occur. Showing them that you are aware about current affairs in software industries can be a plus. When I again entered the TPO hall, I saw my watch, at wasn’t even 11:00 and I was done with 2 rounds already. As 2nd round was HR I was confused if I would be called for 3rd round. I was worried about my performance in 2nd round. After some time, I left the stress producing tpo hall, went for a wake, had my lunch and everything. In Afternoon, students were started calling for the 3rd round. The people who gave 2nd round to X after me were called but not me. This was worrying now. They were asking puzzles in 3rd round. I hadn’t practiced enough of them so I was asking others for which puzzles they were asked and looking for solutions. I was preparing and talking to others and someone came and said we are done with the interviews today. I was sad but I knew that GS take students from 2nd round itself too. Results: The hr was leaving but Swapnil sir convinced her to declare results there itself. She started taking names one after another increasing my impatience and anxiety. Then she said Mohammed .. (couldn’t pronounce my surname) I took a breath of relief and said no need to say surname. After 6 names, she said we are done. One of our friends wasn’t selected so felt a bit for him. I Thanked God and called at home. I think I was lucky for GS, others gave more rounds, answered more questions but everyone has a unique journey. Yuvraj Singh started playing for India at age of 19 but MS Dhoni got his first chance at 23 after a lot of struggles and working as a TC. He was skilled enough but he had to go through the extra struggle because the universe wanted him to make the Caption Cool. The universe wanted him to prepare for tougher situations. So life doesn’t end with one rejection, Jack Ma the Chinese Tycoon, faced 30 rejections for finding a job but went on to build Alibaba. One of my friends was rejected in last rounds of 6 companies located in Hyd, Bang, Pune etc because the 7th company was at 10 min distance to his house in Mumbai. Read interview experience of Sarid Qureshi at Morgan Stanley. During my interview prep, I was also worried and reading through interview experience of seniors, I found these points. Key takeaways: 1. Building a strong resume is crucial, and it’s important to focus only on the skills and technologies you’re truly comfortable with. Don’t forget to seek feedback from seniors to make improvements, and try to increase your ATS score to enhance your chances of getting shortlisted. 2. During interviews, it’s essential to communicate your thought process clearly. Speaking out loud while solving problems not only helps interviewers follow your logic but also gives them the opportunity to provide hints if you're heading in the wrong direction. It’s equally important to mention edge cases during problem-solving, as it shows your thorough approach to tackling challenges. 3. Make sure to practice core computer science concepts like DSA, OOPS, and DBMS regularly. Companies may begin their recruitment process during vacations, so being consistently prepared will give you an advantage. Also, stay on top of CS fundamentals to ensure you’re ready when the opportunity arises. 4. While technical skills are a must, how you express them matters just as much. When you’re unsure or nervous, take a deep breath, and don’t hesitate to ask the interviewer for clarification. It demonstrates that you’re thinking critically before answering, rather than rushing. 5. At CoC, we have mock interviews conducted by seniors, which were incredibly helpful for practicing and receiving constructive feedback before facing the real deal. These mock sessions gave me a chance to refine my skills in a more relaxed environment. 6. Lastly, reading through other candidates’ interview experiences can provide valuable insights, as interview formats are often similar across companies. This will help you better understand what to expect and how to approach different interview stages. Preparation Tips 1. Technical aspect you have to prepare, no doubt in that. But make sure you prepare on your communication skills and there’s only one way to do it and its practice. Talk to people, strangers, your teachers, higher authorities, take any opportunity of public speaking. 2. Practice important DSA topics well in advance. While solving DSA questions, have a time bound and speak up your approach like you are talking to an interviewer 3. Refer 30-40 important questions list on GFG/Interview Bit for OS, DBMS, OOPS. ChatGPT can be very helpful for solving doubts and explaining key concepts. 4. During interview try to speak whatever you think, long silence can be boring for the interviewer. 5. Body language is important, so have an upright, confident posture during the interview. Conclusion With this I will end my interview experience here, I hope it was fun and engaging. If you have any questions regarding my GS interview experience or need advice on interview preparation, feel free to reach out to me at mhdbhadsorawala@gmail.com. I’ll be happy to help as soon as I can. ALL THE BEST!!!
